summary: Former fire lookout in Chesapeake, Virginia, listed as removed. No source found describes what remains on the hill today.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed or gone. No source gives a removal date or describes the site today.

evidence.supports: Listed under the City of Chesapeake
Status removed; the page gives nothing else

evidence.quote: Bowers Hill Chesapeake (City of) 36.78812 -76.41062 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Name attached to the area as early as the 19th century
evidence.quote: the name Bower's Hill was attached to the area as early as the 19th century

evidence.supports: Hill is one of the highest features for miles around
evidence.quote: as one of the highest features for miles around

evidence.supports: Area is generally low-lying coastal plain, so the hill is a high point in otherwise low, flat country
evidence.quote: generally low-lying sandy terrain of the coastal plain

evidence.supports: Wikipedia spells the community Bower's Hill
evidence.quote: Bower's Hill is a community located in the independent city of Chesapeake, Virginia
In 1963, the voters of Norfolk County and the independent city of South Norfolk chose to consolidate into a new city, and Chesapeake was formed.

evidence.supports: Community still rural in 1963; became a borough
evidence.quote: Still-rural Bower's Hill became a borough of the new city.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The lookout lists spell the name Bowers Hill; Wikipedia's community article spells it Bower's Hill. Treated as the same place. The record keeps Bowers Hill.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. The Forest Lookouts page has only the city, the word Removed and no coordinates; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives the status and coordinates. No source found gives a build date, staffing, fire history or removal date, so none is stated. Story is about 180 words. Wikipedia is cited for the community context only, not for the tower.
